content:
# Tasks Document

Ordering is load-bearing. The design's Implementation Order section names six sets that are individually safe and jointly breaking; those constraints are restated inline as **BLOCKING** notes. `tsconfig.json` includes `src/**/*` and `npm run build` runs bare `tsc`, so a partially-applied type change fails the build, not just the tests.

- [ ] 1. Add git resolution primitives with a scrubbed environment
  - File: src/core/git-utils.ts
  - Add `gitCommonDirAbsolute(cwd)` returning `realpath(resolve(cwd, raw))` with no parent-stripping, `gitTopLevel(cwd)` returning null when the command fails, `sameRepository(a, b)` returning false when either side is null, and `normalizeIdentityPath(p)`
  - Delete `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` from the env of every git call in the module, including the existing `resolveGitRoot` and `resolveGitWorkspaceRoot` calls
  - Resolve `SPEC_WORKFLOW_SHARED_ROOT` to an absolute path in `resolveGitRoot` instead of returning it verbatim
  - Purpose: Give inference a correct same-repository test that an inherited environment cannot subvert
  - _Leverage: src/core/git-utils.ts (existing timeout and try/catch conventions), src/core/task-diff.ts:23-27 (env-shaping shape)_
  - _Requirements: 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.9, 2.9_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Add gitCommonDirAbsolute, gitTopLevel, sameRepository and normalizeIdentityPath to src/core/git-utils.ts per requirements 1.4-1.7, 1.9 and 2.9, scrubbing the four GIT_* variables from every git invocation in the module and absolutizing SPEC_WORKFLOW_SHARED_ROOT. | Restrictions: Do NOT reuse the normalization at git-utils.ts:60-66 for the new helpers — it strips .git and returns the repository root, which makes a submodule compare equal to its superproject; compare common directories directly, never a derived parent. sameRepository must return false when either side is null so two non-git directories are not treated as one repository. Keep resolveGitRoot's exported signature unchanged. | _Leverage: existing GIT_EXEC_OPTIONS and try/catch fallbacks in git-utils.ts | _Requirements: 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.9, 2.9 | Success: Unit tests cover repo root, subdirectory at depth, linked worktree, nested worktree, submodule, bare repository, --separate-git-dir, .git-as-file, symlinked root and non-git; a symlinked root compares equal to its own linked worktree; a superproject and submodule compare unequal; with GIT_DIR exported to an unrelated repository two unrelated paths compare unequal; gitTopLevel returns null in a bare repo and inside .git. Set this task to [-] in tasks.md before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 2. Add resolveWorkspaceRoots and wire it into argument parsing
  - Files: src/core/git-utils.ts, src/index.ts, src/__tests__/index-args.test.ts
  - Implement the precedence chain: `SPEC_WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE` (skipped in dashboard mode) → `--no-workspace-inference` → inference → `resolveGitWorkspaceRoot(configuredPath)`
  - Gate inference on `sameRepository` AND a successful `gitTopLevel` on both sides; validate an inferred path with `validateProjectPath` and fall back with a log on failure
  - Validate the environment override with `stat().isDirectory()`, fall through to inference on failure, and warn when it names a different repository
  - Replace the existing log block at src/index.ts:218-225 with one emission fired when `source === 'inference'`
  - Purpose: Make identity resolution one decision point that cannot break a working non-worktree setup
  - _Leverage: src/core/path-utils.ts (validateProjectPath), src/index.ts:180-181 (current resolution), task 1's helpers_
  - _Requirements: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.8, 1.14, 1.15, 1.18, 2.1-2.8, 2.10, 2.11_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Add resolveWorkspaceRoots to src/core/git-utils.ts and replace the resolution at src/index.ts:180-181 with a single call to it, per requirements 1.1-1.3, 1.8, 1.14-1.15, 1.18 and 2.1-2.11. | Restrictions: BLOCKING — src/__tests__/index-args.test.ts declares a vi.mock factory with exactly two git-utils exports; adding an import to index.ts without extending that factory throws every test in the file. Its four assertions pin the current call graph and must be re-derived. The fallback MUST be resolveGitWorkspaceRoot(configuredPath), not the raw configured path — returning the raw path moves projectId, narrows containment to a subdirectory, and breaks parity for users with no worktrees. dashboardMode must be a separate input from noInference, because it suppresses the environment override too and the environment outranks the flag. | _Leverage: validateProjectPath in path-utils.ts, task 1's gitTopLevel and sameRepository | _Requirements: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.8, 1.14, 1.15, 1.18, 2.1-2.8, 2.10, 2.11 | Success: The full precedence matrix is tested; the fallback returns the git toplevel; inference does not fire when either toplevel lookup fails; an inferred path failing validateProjectPath falls back with a log; a non-directory environment value falls through; a different-repository value warns; index-args.test.ts passes with a complete mock factory. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 3. Register the --no-workspace-inference flag at every parse site
  - File: src/index.ts
  - Add the flag to `validFlags` (:115), the argument filter (:166-175), a boolean read alongside the existing flags (:109-111), the return type and `main()` destructure (:99-108, :212-215), and the `--help` OPTIONS block (:26-36)
  - Change the filter to strip any recognised flag in either bare or `=value` form
  - Purpose: Make the flag usable and stop `--flag=value` forms becoming the project path
  - _Leverage: src/index.ts:109-175 (existing flag handling for --no-open and --no-shared-worktree-specs)_
  - _Requirements: 1.16, 1.17_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Register --no-workspace-inference at all five parse sites in src/index.ts and fix the =value filtering hole, per requirements 1.16 and 1.17. | Restrictions: Omitting the validFlags entry does not merely misparse the path — the validation loop at :116-128 throws Unknown option and the server refuses to start, so all five sites are required. The =value fix applies to --no-open and --no-shared-worktree-specs as well, since the loop accepts that form by flag name while the filter matches exact strings only; do not fix it for one flag alone. | _Leverage: existing flag handling at src/index.ts:109-175 | _Requirements: 1.16, 1.17 | Success: The flag parses in bare form and suppresses inference; --no-workspace-inference=true does not become the project path; the same holds for the two pre-existing flags; --help lists the new flag. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 4. Make ToolContext.workspacePath required and update all twenty construction sites
  - Files: src/types.ts, src/server.ts, src/dashboard/multi-server.ts, src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts, plus sixteen test sites across ten files
  - Add `workspacePath: string` as a required field; annotate the literal at src/server.ts:95-99 as `ToolContext`; change `setupHandlers(context: any)` at :135 to `context: ToolContext`
  - Update the inline literals at src/dashboard/multi-server.ts:828 and :969, and src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:100
  - Replace `{} as ToolContext` assertions in fixtures with real values
  - Purpose: Make the required field an enforced contract rather than a convention
  - _Leverage: src/server.ts:61 (the workspace path already held), the compiler itself as the enumeration mechanism_
  - _Requirements: 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Make ToolContext.workspacePath required and update every construction site, per requirements 3.1-3.4. | Restrictions: BLOCKING and INDIVISIBLE — tsconfig.json includes src/**/* and npm run build runs bare tsc, so any intermediate state fails the build. This must be one commit. Adding the field alone produces 19 errors and server.ts is NOT among them, because setupHandlers(context: any) launders the unannotated literal; both the annotation and the parameter type are required or the enforcement does not reach the one site whose omission reproduces the defect. Do NOT silence fixtures with `{} as ToolContext` — an assertion compiles and passes undefined at runtime, which is the silent default requirement 3.1 forbids. Run tsc to enumerate the sites rather than working from a list. | _Leverage: src/server.ts:61 | _Requirements: 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 | Success: tsc is clean; server.ts:96 was among the errors before the fix; no fixture uses a type assertion to satisfy the field; every context carries a real workspace path. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 5. Move safeRealpath into core and surface the error code
  - Files: src/core/file-resolution.ts (new), src/tools/review-task.ts, src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts
  - Move `safeRealpath`, its `warnOnce` set, and `_resetValidateWarnings` from src/tools/review-task.ts:16-39 into the new core module
  - Change the return to a discriminated union carrying the errno on failure, keeping the existing warn policy (silent on ENOENT, warn otherwise) unchanged
  - Purpose: Make ENOENT distinguishable from other failures, without which the drop accounting and the deleted-file guard are unimplementable
  - _Leverage: src/tools/review-task.ts:26-39 (current implementation and warn policy)_
  - _Requirements: 4.10_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Move safeRealpath into src/core/file-resolution.ts and change its return to expose the error code, per requirement 4.10. | Restrictions: BLOCKING — this must land with task 6, because the resolver depends on it. safeRealpath is exported and has its own committed test block including an ELOOP message assertion; that block moves with it and its assertions must still pass. Do NOT change the warn policy: ENOENT stays silent, every other code still warns once with the existing message. A core module must not import from src/tools/, which is why the function moves rather than being imported upward. | _Leverage: the current implementation at src/tools/review-task.ts:26-39 | _Requirements: 4.10 | Success: safeRealpath returns a result carrying the errno on failure; ENOENT is silent and ELOOP warns with the unchanged message; the moved test block passes; no core module imports from src/tools/. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 6. Implement resolveLoggedFiles with anchoring, classification and drop accounting
  - Files: src/core/file-resolution.ts, src/core/__tests__/file-resolution.test.ts
  - Anchor relative entries against the workspace then the workflow root; classify absolute entries by containment only, never anchoring them
  - Mark ambiguous only for relative entries that anchor under both roots
  - Count the six drop causes the code distinguishes: non-array input, non-string element, `path.resolve` throw, ENOENT, non-ENOENT realpath failure, containment rejection
  - Drop an entry whose workspace resolution fails with ENOENT but whose workflow-root resolution succeeds, rather than substituting
  - Establish containment via `validatePathWithinBases` against the workspace and `join(workflowRoot, '.spec-workflow')`, with both bases realpath-normalized
  - Purpose: Resolve logged paths against the right tree and report honestly what could not be resolved
  - _Leverage: src/core/path-utils.ts (validatePathWithinBases), src/dashboard/approval-storage.ts:204-239 (existing workspace-first-then-workflow-root ordering), task 5's safeRealpath_
  - _Requirements: 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.11, 4.12, 4.13, 4.14, 4.15_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Implement resolveLoggedFiles in src/core/file-resolution.ts per requirements 4.6-4.9 and 4.11-4.15. | Restrictions: Anchoring and classification are DIFFERENT operations — path.resolve ignores its base for an absolute argument, so a single resolve-against-each-root function is a no-op for absolute entries and would mark every one of them ambiguous. Absolute entries must not be anchored at all. Containment must never accept the workflow root itself: in a nested layout that root contains every sibling worktree. Both containment bases must be realpath-normalized, since resolved paths are — comparing a normalized path against an unnormalized base rejects every .spec-workflow path under a symlinked workflow root. Reuse validatePathWithinBases rather than reimplementing containment. | _Leverage: validatePathWithinBases, ApprovalStorage.getFilePathCandidates ordering, task 5's safeRealpath | _Requirements: 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.11, 4.12, 4.13, 4.14, 4.15 | Success: A bare relative path resolves to the workspace; absolute paths under each root are classified correctly and asserted NOT ambiguous; a relative path anchoring under both is ambiguous; all six drop causes are counted separately; a file deleted in the workspace but present in the workflow root is dropped as missing, not substituted; ENOENT drops emit no warning; containment accepts .spec-workflow above the workspace and rejects a sibling worktree in a nested layout, including under a symlinked workflow root. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 7. Delete the pre-resolution and wire the resolver into handlePrepare
  - Files: src/tools/review-task.ts, src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts
  - Delete the `.map(p => path.resolve(projectPath, p))` at src/tools/review-task.ts:360-361, keeping the `new Set` dedupe at :360; pass raw log entries to `resolveLoggedFiles`
  - Replace `validateAllFiles` with the new resolver and update its ten test call sites and two `warnOnce` message assertions
  - Route `workspaceFiles` to the diff, the typecheck and the hygiene signals; keep spec, steering, settings and workflow-root reads on the workflow root
  - Purpose: Make code operations read the worktree while spec reads stay shared
  - _Leverage: task 6's resolveLoggedFiles, src/tools/review-task.ts:380-391 (current call sites)_
  - _Requirements: 4.1, 4.5, 4.20, 4.21, 4.22_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Delete the path pre-resolution at src/tools/review-task.ts:360-361 and wire resolveLoggedFiles into handlePrepare, per requirements 4.1, 4.5 and 4.20-4.22. | Restrictions: BLOCKING — the deletion must NOT land after the two-root partition. Deleting the .map alone is safe because the resolver re-anchors against the workflow root, matching today; the reverse order silently resolves every relative entry against the wrong tree and then drops it on containment. Keep the new Set dedupe at :360. validateAllFiles is exported and has ten test call sites all passing a string second argument and asserting a flat array; decide and state what containment rejection warns, since the current message names projectPath and there are now two roots. | _Leverage: task 6's resolveLoggedFiles | _Requirements: 4.1, 4.5, 4.20, 4.21, 4.22 | Success: Bare relative log entries resolve to the workspace; .spec-workflow entries resolve to the workflow root and reach filesToReview but not the diff, typecheck or hygiene inputs; spec, steering and settings still read from the workflow root; all ten migrated test call sites pass. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 8. Split the typecheck root so cache and ignore writes stay shared
  - Files: src/core/typecheck.ts, src/tools/review-task.ts
  - Add a second root parameter: use the workspace for `tsconfigPath` and `resolveTscBinary`, and the workflow root for the cache mkdir (:139-140) and `ensureGitignoreEntry` (:141)
  - Ensure `unwrapTypecheck` (src/tools/review-task.ts:391) reports `tsconfigPath` from the workspace so every result arm agrees
  - Purpose: Typecheck the worktree without creating .spec-workflow in it or dirtying its tracked .gitignore
  - _Leverage: src/core/typecheck.ts:113, :134, :139-141 (current single-root uses)_
  - _Requirements: 4.2, 4.3_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Give runProjectTypecheck a second root parameter so tsconfig and compiler resolution use the workspace while the cache directory and the git-ignore entry use the workflow root, per requirements 4.2 and 4.3. | Restrictions: Passing the workspace for all uses would create a .spec-workflow directory inside every worktree — contradicting the premise that .spec-workflow is shared — and leave each worktree with an uncommitted edit to its tracked .gitignore. unwrapTypecheck builds tsconfigPath from its root argument and must receive the workspace, or the rejection arm reports a different root from every other arm while requirement 3.11 pins tsconfigPath as a parity observable. | _Leverage: src/core/typecheck.ts:113, :134, :139-141 | _Requirements: 4.2, 4.3 | Success: A typecheck in a worktree resolves that worktree's tsconfig and compiler; no .spec-workflow directory appears in the worktree; the workflow root's .gitignore is the only one touched; tsconfigPath is identical across success, unavailable and rejection arms; with equal roots behaviour is unchanged. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 9. Add the minimal file-resolution disclosure and carry it to both review paths
  - Files: src/tools/review-task.ts, src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts
  - Add `fileResolution: { workspaceCount, workflowCount, drops, note? }` to the prepare response, setting `note` when the workspace set is empty while the task logged files
  - Add `fileResolution` to the destructure at src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:110 and to `buildPrompt`, rendering it before the file list
  - Purpose: Stop an all-drop review reaching the agent as an empty list with a fabricated explanation
  - _Leverage: src/tools/review-task.ts:410-424 (prepare response), src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:110, :138_
  - _Requirements: 4.16_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Add the minimal file-resolution disclosure to the prepare response and carry it through the runner into the review prompt, per requirement 4.16. | Restrictions: The runner destructures five fields from an any-typed prepareResponse.data at :110 and discards the rest, so a field added to the response does NOT reach the dashboard-spawned reviewer unless :110 and buildPrompt are both updated — and the compiler will not catch the omission. Without this, an all-drop review reaches the agent as an empty file list under an instruction to read every file in it, alongside R4_2A_DIFF_EMPTY's claim that the changes were already committed. Keep this minimal — counts and one note string, not the structured execution-context object, which belongs to worktree-review-signals. | _Leverage: src/tools/review-task.ts:410-424, src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:110, :138 | _Requirements: 4.16 | Success: An all-drop prepare returns a note; that note appears in the prompt built for a dashboard-triggered review as well as to a direct caller; counts reflect the six drop causes. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 10. Update the file-list shape through buildPrompt
  - Files: src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts, src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts
  - Change `buildPrompt`'s `filesToReview` parameter (:212) and its rendering (:277) to carry the per-path root label, and update the two committed assertions on the flat shape
  - Purpose: Let the reviewing agent tell reviewable code from spec documents it is told to open
  - _Leverage: src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:212, :277_
  - _Requirements: 4.15, 4.17_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Update buildPrompt's filesToReview parameter and rendering to carry the per-path root label, per requirements 4.15 and 4.17. | Restrictions: BLOCKING — this must land with the shape change itself. buildPrompt types the parameter string[] and renders it with .map, receiving it from an any-typed destructure, so a shape change produces NO build error and the prompt silently renders one object placeholder per file. Two committed assertions pin the flat shape and must be updated in the same change. | _Leverage: src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:212, :277 | _Requirements: 4.15, 4.17 | Success: The rendered prompt shows each file with its root; no object placeholders appear; the two migrated assertions pass; a dashboard-triggered review is inspected to confirm the rendering. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 11. Add selectRoots and apply it to the four root-sensitive tools
  - Files: src/tools/root-selection.ts (new), src/tools/review-task.ts, src/tools/log-implementation.ts, src/tools/adversarial-review.ts, src/tools/adversarial-response.ts
  - Return the context's roots with no override; with an override return it as the workspace and derive the workflow root from it, warning and naming the discarded context value
  - Warn when the derivation degrades to the override verbatim, and memoize the derivation per override value
  - Purpose: Stop an override reintroducing the wrong-root defect on the tool-argument path
  - _Leverage: src/core/git-utils.ts (resolveGitRoot), existing warnOnce usage in review-task.ts_
  - _Requirements: 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8, 3.9, 3.10_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Add selectRoots and apply it at the four override sites named in requirement 3.8, per requirements 3.5-3.10. | Restrictions: Taking an override verbatim as the workflow root makes .spec-workflow lookups search inside a worktree — the defect requirement 3.6 exists to prevent. resolveGitRoot returns its input unchanged in four cases (SPEC_WORKFLOW_SHARED_ROOT set, the git call failing, a common dir with no .git substring as under --separate-git-dir, and a bare repository returning '.'), so the derivation silently degrades to verbatim and must warn. The derivation is a synchronous execSync with a five-second timeout, so memoize per override value. Apply only to review-task, log-implementation, adversarial-review and adversarial-response; the other override-accepting tools read only .spec-workflow and are out of scope by criterion. | _Leverage: resolveGitRoot, existing warnOnce | _Requirements: 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8, 3.9, 3.10 | Success: With no override the context roots pass through; with an override the workflow root is derived and a warning names both paths; each of the four degradation cases warns; repeated calls with one override value invoke git once. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 12. Give TaskReviewRunner two named roots and update both its routes
  - Files: src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts, src/dashboard/multi-server.ts
  - Replace the single `projectPath` in `RunOptions` with `workflowRoot` and `workspacePath`; use the workflow root at :95 and for `ToolContext.projectPath` at :100, and the workspace for the spawn cwd at :144 → :365
  - Update the task-review route (:1791) and the retry route (:1853) to pass both
  - Purpose: Let the review agent start in the worktree while still finding the shared spec
  - _Leverage: src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:27-35, :95, :100, :144, :365_
  - _Requirements: 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.6_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Split TaskReviewRunner.RunOptions into workflowRoot and workspacePath and update both task-review routes, per requirements 5.1-5.4 and 5.6. | Restrictions: BLOCKING — the option change must land with both routes (:1791 and :1853) or the dashboard passes a field that no longer exists. The single projectPath is currently spent three incompatible ways: getSpecPath at :95 needs the workflow root, the ToolContext at :100 needs both, and the spawn cwd at :144 needs the workspace. Setting it to the workspace makes getSpecPath resolve a .spec-workflow inside the worktree and every review fails with tasks.md not found. | _Leverage: src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:27-35, :95, :100, :144, :365 | _Requirements: 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.6 | Success: getSpecPath resolves against the workflow root; the spawned child's cwd is the workspace; the ToolContext carries both; both routes compile and pass both roots. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 13. Fix both adversarial routes and AdversarialRunner's single field
  - Files: src/dashboard/adversarial-runner.ts, src/dashboard/multi-server.ts
  - Rename `AdversarialRunner.RunOptions.projectPath` to `workspacePath`, documenting that the runner needs only one root because it never resolves a spec path or builds a ToolContext
  - Pass the workflow root to `adversarialReviewHandler` at :828 and :969, and the translated workspace to the runner at :852 and :1012
  - Purpose: Stop the adversarial routes searching for their target document inside a worktree
  - _Leverage: src/dashboard/adversarial-runner.ts:111, src/tools/adversarial-review.ts:60_
  - _Requirements: 5.5, 5.7, 5.8_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Rename AdversarialRunner's path field to workspacePath and fix all four adversarial call sites, per requirements 5.5, 5.7 and 5.8. | Restrictions: There are TWO adversarial routes, not one — the review route (:828 handler, :852 runner) and the retry route (:969 handler, :1012 runner) — and the retry route reproduces both defects verbatim. adversarialReviewHandler immediately calls PathUtils.getWorkflowRoot on what it receives, so passing a workspace path makes it search inside the worktree and fail to find the target document; the handler sites need the workflow root. The runner sites need project.workspacePath, not originalProjectPath, so the path is Docker-translated like every other runner path. Do NOT add a second field to AdversarialRunner: it uses its path at exactly one place and a workflowRoot field would be dead. | _Leverage: src/dashboard/adversarial-runner.ts:111, src/tools/adversarial-review.ts:60 | _Requirements: 5.5, 5.7, 5.8 | Success: An adversarial review triggered from a worktree locates its target document; so does a retry; both runners spawn in the worktree; the runner carries one path field. Set this task to [-] before starting, call log-implementation when done, then mark it [x]._

- [ ] 14. Scrub GIT_* from code-path git invocations and add the diff containment assertion
  - Files: src/core/task-diff.ts, src/core/typecheck.ts, src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts, src/dashboard/adversarial-runner.ts
  - Delete the four `GIT_*` variables from `runGit`'s env (src/core/task-diff.ts:23-27), from the typecheck spawn env (:153), and from both agent spawn envs (:368, :147), setting the two `SPEC_WORKFLOW_*` roots explicitly at the spawn sites and preserving the path-translation prefixes
  - Assert every diff pathspec is contained by the workspace before invoking git, and set `TaskDiffResult.rejection` when the assertion fails
  - Purpose: Stop an inherited environment silently making git read another repository
  - _Leverage: src/core/task-diff.ts:9 (existing rejection field), :23-27 (env shaping)_
  - _Requirements: 2.12, 2.13, 4.18, 4.19_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec worktree-execution-context, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Task: Scrub the four GIT_* variables from the three code-path git invocation sites and add the pre-invocation containment assertion, per requirements 2.12, 2.13, 4.18 and 4.19. | Restrictions: runGit at src/core/task-diff.ts:23-27 sets env to a spread of process.env plus GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS — it inherits wholesale and scrubs nothing, and it runs in the PARENT process so neither spawn-site scrub reaches it.
